title: core: Envelope.applyTo() ignores oscillator gain, ramps attack to absolute 1.0
description:
Envelope.applyTo() in packages/core/src/envelope.ts (line ~194) always ramps the attack phase to an absolute peak of 1.0 via gainParam.linearRampToValueAtTime(1, attackEndTime), regardless of the oscillator's configured _targetGain. The decay phase similarly ramps to the raw sustain ratio (0-1) rather than sustain*_targetGain. This means any oscillator created with both a 'gain' option and an 'envelope' option gets an attack peak of 1.0 no matter how low 'gain' is set — the gain option is silently ignored whenever an envelope is present.

Impact: recurring demo-layer friction. Confirmed workarounds needed in AmbientGenerator.vue (avoids ADSR envelope entirely) and EffectsChainDemo.vue (uses onPlaySet('gain') manual scheduling instead of the envelope constructor option — see its triggerPatternNote/comment at lines 64-70). Most recently caused a real clipping regression in TransportSequencerDemo.vue (loudness E2E measured peak 1.05-1.06, threshold is 0.985) until the same onPlaySet workaround was applied there too (see .superpowers/sdd/task-7-report.md).

Proposed fix: scale the envelope's target values by _targetGain in Envelope.applyTo() (and triggerRelease() if applicable) — ramp attack to 1 * targetGain, decay to sustain * targetGain — rather than raw 0-1 absolute values. Requires passing _targetGain into the Envelope instance/methods, or having the calling controller (e.g. OscillatorController.setValuesAtTimes()) scale the envelope curve by gain before calling applyTo().

Already flagged in project memory (MEMORY.md) as 'strongest pre-1.0 core API candidate' — this issue formalizes it as trackable work. Fix belongs in packages/core, not per-demo workarounds.
